subject: pharmacology
title: ACE Inhibitors: Captopril, Enalapril, Lisinopril and Ramipril

steps.tx: The short acting sulfhydryl containing prototype that first proved angiotensin converting enzyme blockade works is **captopril**. The enzyme it blocks converts angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and simultaneously breaks down bradykinin. Inhibiting it therefore dilates arterioles, cuts aldosterone release and lets bradykinin accumulate. Captopril needs two or three doses daily and is taken on an empty stomach because food cuts its absorption.
steps.say: Captopril blocks the converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II while letting bradykinin build up.

vis.caption: The renin angiotensin cascade with the ACE step blocked, showing vasodilatation and the fetal kidney warning. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Most successors are **prodrugs** activated by hepatic esterases: enalapril becomes enalaprilat, ramipril becomes ramiprilat, and perindopril becomes perindoprilat. Lisinopril breaks the pattern as the active lysine analogue of enalaprilat, absorbed unchanged and excreted by the kidney. Active metabolites bind tissue ACE tightly and clear slowly, which is why once daily dosing controls pressure around the clock despite shorter plasma half lives.
steps.say: Enalapril and ramipril need liver activation; lisinopril is active as swallowed. All of them grip tissue ACE for a full day.

left.title: Prodrug ACE inhibitors
points: Enalapril converted to enalaprilat in the liver
Ramipril converted to ramiprilat, very tight tissue binding
Inactive in renal failure only if liver activation fails rarely
Once daily dosing from slow tissue ACE dissociation

right.title: Active as given
points: Captopril active, short acting, food reduces absorption
Lisinopril active lysine analogue, renally excreted
Enalaprilat itself used intravenously in emergencies abroad
Renal dose adjustment needed for lisinopril in kidney disease

steps.tx: Falling angiotensin II removes feedback inhibition on the juxtaglomerular apparatus, so plasma **renin** activity rises severalfold on treatment. That rise is expected and harmless, but it means the system is primed: stop the drug and angiotensin II rebounds. The same feedback explains why combining an ACE inhibitor with a direct renin inhibitor or a receptor blocker stacks adverse effects faster than it adds blood pressure benefit.
steps.say: Renin rises on ACE inhibitors because the brake is off; that is expected, and it warns against stacking blockers.

nodes.label: ACE inhibitor blocks angiotensin II formation
Negative feedback on juxtaglomerular cells lost
Renin release and plasma renin activity climb
Dual blockade risks hypotension and hyperkalaemia

steps.tx: In **hypertension** these drugs lower pressure without reflex tachycardia, because angiotensin II withdrawal also reduces sympathetic facilitation and resets baroreceptors. They are preferred starters with diabetes, proteinuria or left ventricular hypertrophy, and they regress hypertrophy better than pressure matched beta blockade. A first dose fall is most likely in salt depleted or high renin patients, so the opening dose is small and diuretics are sometimes paused for a day.
steps.say: Pressure falls without a racing heart, ventricles remodel backwards, and the first dose deserves respect.

left.title: Haemodynamic profile
points: Arteriolar dilatation lowers afterload
Venodilatation and natriuresis trim preload
No reflex tachycardia or fluid retention
Cerebral and renal autoregulation preserved

right.title: First dose precautions
points: Start low in diuretic treated or salt depleted patients
Check creatinine and potassium within two weeks
A creatinine rise up to 30 percent can be acceptable
Larger rises suggest renal artery stenosis or volume depletion

steps.tx: After myocardial infarction, early ACE inhibition limits infarct expansion and adverse remodelling, while in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction agents such as **ramipril** and enalapril cut mortality and hospitalisation. Benefit tracks with dose, so guidelines push titration toward trial doses as pressure, potassium and creatinine allow. The same afterload and aldosterone reduction slows progression of diabetic kidney disease discussed in the companion hyperkalaemia lesson.
steps.say: Post infarct and in heart failure these drugs save lives; titrate toward trial doses as labs allow.

nodes.label: Infarction or reduced ejection fraction heart failure
Start ACE inhibitor early at low dose
Uptitrate toward trial doses over weeks
Less remodelling, fewer deaths and admissions

steps.tx: The signature nuisance is a persistent dry **cough** in 5 to 15 percent of patients, more in women and in East Asian populations, caused by bradykinin and substance P accumulating in airways. It starts weeks into therapy, disturbs sleep, and resolves within days to weeks of stopping. Rechallenge reproduces it, so the correct move is switching class, usually to an angiotensin receptor blocker, rather than suppressing it with antitussives.
steps.say: A dry cough weeks into treatment is bradykinin talking; switch class instead of treating the cough.

left.title: ACE inhibitor cough
points: Dry, tickly, worse lying flat at night
Onset weeks to months after starting
Bradykinin and substance P accumulate in bronchi
Resolves on withdrawal, recurs on rechallenge

right.title: Cough not to blame on the drug
points: Productive cough with fever suggests infection
Wheeze and breathlessness suggest asthma or failure
Haemoptysis always needs its own workup
Check the timeline before blaming the tablet

steps.tx: Bradykinin excess also explains **angioedema**, the rarest but most dangerous reaction, with sudden swelling of lips, tongue and larynx that can obstruct the airway. Risk is several fold higher in Black patients, and episodes can strike after years of uneventful use. It does not respond reliably to antihistamines or steroids because it is bradykinin rather than histamine mediated; securing the airway comes first, and the class is banned for life afterwards.
steps.say: Angioedema on an ACE inhibitor means airway first, drug banned for life, and no rechallenge ever.

left.title: Bradykinin angioedema
points: Lips, tongue and larynx swell over hours
No urticaria or itch accompanies the swelling
Antihistamines and steroids are unreliable
Airway assessment and monitoring come first

right.title: Immediate actions
points: Stop the ACE inhibitor permanently
Assess airway, give oxygen, call for airway help
Observe for at least 12 to 24 hours after an episode
Document drug allergy prominently for all future prescribers

steps.tx: Captopril carries two quirks from its **sulfhydryl** group that later agents largely escaped: a metallic taste disturbance and, at the high doses of early practice, neutropenia and proteinuria resembling penicillamine toxicity. Modern low doses make these rare, but the exam still pairs captopril with taste loss, rash and the shortest half life in the class. It remains useful where a brief, quickly reversible trial of ACE blockade is wanted.
steps.say: Captopril alone carries the sulfhydryl quirks: metallic taste, rash, and rare marrow and kidney toxicity at high dose.

left.title: Captopril specifics
points: Sulfhydryl group, active without liver activation
Half life under 2 hours, dosed two or three times daily
Food reduces absorption, take before meals
Taste disturbance and rash are class distinctive

right.title: Class wide effects
points: Dry cough and rare angioedema from bradykinin
Hyperkalaemia and creatinine rise from aldosterone fall
Fetopathy in second and third trimester exposure
Hypotension in volume depleted or high renin states

steps.tx: Practical prescribing runs on three numbers: baseline **potassium**, creatinine and blood pressure, rechecked one to two weeks after starting or increasing the dose. Stop or seek advice for potassium above 5.5 mmol per litre, a creatinine rise beyond 30 percent, symptomatic hypotension, cough that will not settle, or any angioedema. Pregnancy planning means switching beforehand, because the fetal kidney depends on angiotensin II from mid gestation onward.
steps.say: Check potassium, creatinine and pressure before and after starting; know your five stop rules cold.

nodes.label: Start low, counsel on cough and swelling
Recheck labs in one to two weeks
Stop for hyperkalaemia, big creatinine rise or angioedema
